purpose: Priority-1: does sealed pooled AUPRC misrepresent per-structure fit / memorisation?
method: instrumented CUDA replay of sealed E400 G_fit folds; same harness wrapper; no disposition edit
read: Sealed pooled train AUPRC (~0.80-0.83) is a roughly honest training-fit number, not a pooling artifact: macro-mean per-structure AUPRC is HIGHER than pooled (0.828-0.848), and rank-/z-normalised pooling lowers it by only ~0.04-0.05 (small cross-structure score-offset effect). Per-structure train AUPRC ranges 0.63-0.98 (5-6 of 11 structures >=0.90). Held-out AUPRC is 0.48-0.57 vs prevalence 0.39-0.58 (lift 0.97-1.21x, ~chance), so the fit is per-structure memorisation on a coordinate-only path (edge_type has no measurable effect; see edge_type_reachability_check). The E200->E400 chain is moot as a capacity question because of wiring and step budget (Euclidean-skip path, near-frozen frontend, hyperbolic layers not in the dehydron loss graph; see grad_attribution_check), not because the pooled metric is broken. 2026-09-20 amendment: an earlier draft of this line said the pooled headline was inflated and the chain characterised a pooling artifact; recomputation from the saved scores did not support that.
not_claims: not an Arm B disposition edit
implication_for_epoch_budget_chain: E200->E400 decay modelling is moot as a capacity question (wiring + step budget, not metric). G_fit is a train-fit gate, so near-chance held-out is expected and is a memorisation diagnostic, not a G_fit failure. Redesign G_fit (loss through z_hyp; report per-structure + held-out) before any new epoch card. Hold pool typed G_fit and Arm B disposition edit.
